title: 15th Sitting of First session of 2026
presiding: Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Speaker, Fonadhoo); Ahmed Nazim (Deputy Speaker, Dhiggaru) after the 10:29 recess
summary: Most of this part was question time for Dr Abdulla Muttalib, the Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development. Members asked about foreign-funded road works in Malé and the islands, harbours, water and sewerage systems, and housing, including the 4,000 Gedhoruveriya flats, land reclamation at Gulhifalhu, Hulhumalé Phase 3 and Rasmale, and the island registry of people living in rent-to-own flats. The minister said projects funded by China, Japan and India go through each lender's tender, design and approval steps, and said he did not have exact dates for several island projects. Under the Speaker's business, a presidential letter proposing to remove methylphenidate (used to treat ADHD) from the banned-drugs schedule was sent to a committee, and the sitting broke for 30 minutes from 10:29. The sitting resumed with the debate on an MDP resolution asking MPs to give their views on how Public Service Media (PSM) treats parties; MDP and PNC members spoke on both sides, and the sponsor was not in the chamber to wind up. The House then debated a constitutional amendment bill from North Galolhu that aims to bring back the atoll councils, with several members speaking for restoring them. Both the resolution and the bill were put to a vote and neither was accepted, each by 8 votes to 45. The chair then adjourned the sitting until 9:00 on Tuesday 5 May 2026.

speakers.name: Dr. Abdulla Muttalib (Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development)
positions: Said projects funded by China, Japan and India follow each lender's tender, survey, design and contractor steps, so start dates depend on those stages.
Said machinery shortages hold up island works and that he lacked exact dates for several projects, promising to follow up.
Said registering flat residents is the city council's responsibility and that the council had not replied to ministry letters.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked when the China-assisted Malé road upgrade will actually start and how it will ease traffic congestion.
Asked how island registry will work for people living in flats under the rent-to-own agreement with Fahi Dhiriulhun Corporation.
Asked whether any easing was arranged on the advance payment for the 4,000 flats, and raised garbage, mosquito and power-cut problems in the flats.
As sponsor, said councils should return so atoll residents have a say over resources and islands, and urged the government to accept the amendment.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked whether the delay to Malé's road project was deliberate and when work on roads in his own constituency will start.
Asked how long China-assisted design and build will take before practical work can begin.
Asked how the remaining eligible applicants for the Gedhoruveriya flats will be housed, and what housing projects are planned in Baa atoll and Kendhoo.
Said councils were abolished over cost and use of funds, argued decentralisation is built into the Constitution, and supported restoring them.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked why Kunahandhoo's water and sewerage work is stalled by labour shortage while many state-company staff are on the island.
Asked for updates on the Laamu causeways, including the Kunahandhoo-Hithadhoo link, and on Rasmale versus work in Laamu.
Said Laamu has received little compared with other atolls and asked for basic services on islands like Kunahandhoo.
Supported the bill; said atolls like Laamu fall behind in services such as health care and lose out when councils are removed.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked how far the Vaikaradhoo harbour work given to MTCC has progressed.
Asked for the status of the jetty planned at Neyalaidhoo harbour for launches.
On the PSM resolution: backed it, saying PSM does not treat parties equally.
On the constitutional bill: backed restoring atoll councils and reversing the earlier amendment.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked when practical work will start on the housing units for Maradhoo signed at a ceremony last year.
Asked whether the ministry plans water, sewerage, power and roads on the newly reclaimed land in Maradhoo, and when.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked for an update on the Addu City link road work.
Asked whether finance or a plan exists to reclaim the plots issued from the sea in Malé area.
Said all governments see PSM differently and that fair rules should apply to all media; argued the resolution takes up Parliament's time unnecessarily.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked when Noomaraa and Bileiyfahi sewerage will finish and whether Bileiyfahi airport can avoid dredging the lagoon.
Asked if Goidhoo and Kanditheemu harbours start this year, why Feydhoo was left out of the road project, and why Rasmale land is being allocated.
Asked whether Noomaraa and Bileiyfahi can get their water and sewerage service this year.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked for a yes or no on whether the city mayor is the one who can register residents of the flats.
Asked how many plots and flats were reclaimed, given and built during the previous government's 15,000 flat and 5,000 plot pledge.
Noted few MDP members were present to debate their own resolution; cited Maldives' press freedom ranking and the weekly and monthly press access given by officials.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked when practical work on the Thoddoo and Rasdhoo roads will start.
Said Thoddoo's road was about 70% done in 2023 and asked when it will be finished.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Asked when practical work on the 300 housing units in Vilimale' will start, citing opposition over tree felling.
Opposed the resolution; said the MDP gets access to PSM and pointed to the 18th Majlis PSM law the MDP itself passed.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Asked whether Maaenboodhoo's water system, contracted under the previous government, could be moved to another contractor given delays.
Asked under which law a new government must hand over land or flats issued contrary to rules.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked why the cost of the new 4,000 flats differs so much from earlier social housing.
Asked whether there is a plan to repair or replace Hulhumalé's Chinese-built flats with structural damage.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Asked when Naivaadhoo's sewerage work will finish and the service become available.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Asked what the plan is for the 100 housing units the President mentioned for Thimarafushi during his Thaa atoll visit.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Abdul Rahman
positions: Asked when the water system on Alifushi will serve residents and when stalled airport work will restart.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Asked how the Huraa harbour work will proceed, and when housing and flat plans on islands near Malé will start.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked when the failing sewerage system in his constituency will be fixed and whether any plan exists.

speakers.name: Ali Ashrag
positions: Asked when sewerage at Kandoodhoo and Omadhoo, and harbour and coast protection at Vandhoo, will start, and what is being done on the Kinbidhoo-Vaymandhoo causeway.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked when work starts on the land reclamation promised for Keyodhoo, and how the Rakeedhoo relocation is progressing.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Asked how long Gulhifalhu and Giraavaru water, sewerage and power work will take.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shifaz
positions: Asked for an update on the 500 housing units promised to address Ungoofaaru's housing problem.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shamin Habeeb
positions: Raised slow progress on Kurendhoo and Olhuvelifushi harbours and asked whether a completion date has been set.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said media freedom has widened under this government but reporting must be responsible, and criticised how some outlets cover protests and the President.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said he could not support the resolution; argued PSM should show national work and that the MDP raised it mainly over coverage of its protests.

decisions: A presidential letter (dated 30 April 2026) proposing to remove methylphenidate from Schedule 1 of the Drugs Act (Law 17/2011) was referred to the Security Services Committee under Rule 127.
The sitting recessed for 30 minutes from 10:29 to 11:01, after which the Deputy Speaker took the chair.
Resolution on PSM and party access (item 7.1) was not accepted at the vote.
Constitutional amendment bill on atoll councils (item 7.2) was not accepted at the vote.
Chair closed debate on 7.1 because no further member asked to speak and the sponsor was absent.
Next sitting set for 9:00 on Tuesday 5 May 2026.

votes.what: Accept resolution on PSM and party access (South Galolhu sponsor)
Accept constitutional amendment bill on atoll councils (North Galolhu sponsor)
